title: An interpretable graph reasoning framework for enhanced diagnosis in fundus fluorescein angiography
_abs_err: springer: Client Challenge (bot check) from citation-needed.springer.c; page: Client Challenge (bot check) from www.nature.com
zh_title: 眼底荧光血管造影可解释图推理诊断框架
summary: 提出可解释图推理框架FFA-RGNet，基于多中心25,312张FFA图像建模病灶时序与解剖模式，内部测试F1达95.38%。

abstract: Fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA) is the gold standard for diagnosing retinal vascular diseases. However, interpretable artificial intelligence (AI) systems for FFA image analysis that align with clinicians’ reasoning processes and real-world diagnostic workflows remain scarce. In this study, we introduce an interpretable graph reasoning framework, FFA-RGNet, that explicitly models the temporal patterns of fine-grained lesions across imaging phases and anatomical locations for disease diagnosis from sequential FFA images. FFA-RGNet was trained and validated on a large, fine-grained, multi-center dataset consisting of 25,312 FFA images from 2651 patients. FFA-RGNet outperformed nine baseline models on the internal test set, achieving an F1-score of 95.38% (95% CI: 92.24%–97.88%), and demonstrated consistent performance across multi-center and prospective validation datasets. Its diagnostic performance not only surpassed that of ophthalmologists, residents and ophthalmology students, but also improved their diagnostic F1-score by 7.48% to 14.11% when used as an assistive tool. Comprehensive inference analysis further revealed its superior ability to correctly recognize fine-grained semantic entities, and to learn stable, disease-specific graph reasoning patterns aligned with clinical knowledge. These results suggest that FFA-RGNet enables accurate diagnosis with interpretable reasoning progresses, highlighting its strong potential as a reliable AI system for FFA interpretation and clinical decision support.
zh_abstract: 眼底荧光素血管造影（fundus fluorescein angiography，FFA）是诊断视网膜血管疾病的金标准。然而，用于FFA图像分析、与临床医生推理过程和真实世界诊断工作流程相一致的可解释人工智能（AI）系统仍然稀缺。在本研究中，我们介绍了一个可解释的图推理框架FFA-RGNet，该框架明确建模细粒度病变在成像阶段和解剖位置上的时间模式，以从序列FFA图像中进行疾病诊断。FFA-RGNet在一个大型、细粒度、多中心数据集上进行了训练和验证，该数据集包含来自2651例患者的25,312张FFA图像。FFA-RGNet在内部测试集上优于九个基线模型，达到95.38%的F1分数（95% CI：92.24%–97.88%），并在多中心和前瞻性验证数据集上表现一致。其诊断性能不仅超过了眼科医生、住院医师和眼科学生，而且作为辅助工具使用时，将其诊断F1分数提高了7.48%至14.11%。全面的推理分析进一步揭示了其正确识别细粒度语义实体以及学习与临床知识一致的、稳定的疾病特异性图推理模式的优越能力。这些结果表明，FFA-RGNet能够以可解释的推理过程实现准确诊断，突显其作为用于FFA解读和临床决策支持的可靠AI系统的强大潜力。

abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into clinical medical imaging has advanced diagnostics but also poses challenges in maintaining long-term reliability as input data change. To address this, we present MMC+, a modular framework for scalable drift monitoring that builds on our CheXstray framework for real-time drift detection using multi-modal data concordance (MMC). MMC+ provides a flexible architecture that enables cost-effective continuous performance monitoring in real-world healthcare settings. The framework’s capabilities include aggregating information from multiple data streams using statistical tests or distance metrics, leveraging foundation model embeddings to remove the need for site-specific encoder training, and quantifying uncertainty to better communicate drift significance. Validated with data from Massachusetts General Hospital during the COVID-19 pandemic, MMC+ effectively detects significant data shifts that correlate with performance changes and indicates when AI systems may deviate from acceptable performance bounds. The code for MMC+ is publicly available (Link: https://github.com/FJDorfner/MedImaging-ModelDriftMonitoring/tree/MMC_plus ), promoting broader adoption of AI solutions in clinical settings. Our framework significantly advances drift detection while promoting transparency and collaboration in clinical AI research.
zh_abstract: 将人工智能（AI）整合到临床医学影像中促进了诊断，但也带来了在输入数据变化时保持长期可靠性的挑战。为解决这一问题，我们提出MMC+，这是一个可扩展漂移监测的模块化框架，建立在我们CheXstray框架之上，该框架利用多模态数据一致性（multi-modal data concordance，MMC）进行实时漂移检测。MMC+提供了一种灵活的架构，可在真实世界医疗环境中实现具有成本效益的持续性能监测。该框架的能力包括：使用统计检验或距离度量聚合来自多个数据流的信息，利用基础模型嵌入以消除对站点特定编码器训练的需求，以及量化不确定性以更好地传达漂移显著性。MMC+在COVID-19大流行期间使用马萨诸塞州总医院（Massachusetts General Hospital）的数据进行了验证，能够有效检测与性能变化相关的显著数据偏移，并指示AI系统何时可能偏离可接受的性能界限。MMC+的代码已公开（链接：https://github.com/FJDorfner/MedImaging-ModelDriftMonitoring/tree/MMC_plus ），促进AI解决方案在临床环境中的更广泛采用。我们的框架显著推进了漂移检测，同时促进了临床AI研究的透明性和合作。

title: MedJev: Evaluating Zero-Shot System-One Decision Making in Medicine
zh_title: MedJev：医学零样本System One决策评测
summary: 预印本在十个医学基准上评测开源System One模型MedJev，报告其在知识问答与院内死亡预测上的表现。
key_points: MedQA 72.5%、USMLE 75.4%、NEJM 80.1%
院内死亡AUROC 0.926，高于XGBoost 0.902

reason: 多基准对比公开模型与监督模型，但为预印本、无临床结局
abstract: System One decision models such as Jev answer structured questions in a single forward pass without generating text, offering fast and computationally efficient clinical decision support. We evaluate MedJev, an open System One model that runs locally on a laptop, across ten medical benchmarks spanning medical knowledge, diagnosis, and patient level prediction using MIMIC IV and MIMIC IV ED. We compare MedJev against zero shot LLM baselines, published GPT results, and supervised models. MedJev achieves accuracies of 72.5 percent on MedQA, 75.4 percent on USMLE, and 80.1 percent on NEJM, approaching published GPT 4 performance while maintaining well calibrated confidence estimates (ECE 0.028 to 0.063). On patient level tasks, MedJev achieves an AUROC of 0.926 for In Hospital Mortality, exceeding XGBoost (0.902), but underperforms supervised models on operational outcomes such as ED Triage Admission (0.745 vs. 0.809). Patient level predictions also exhibit substantial miscalibration (In Hospital Mortality ECE 0.286). We introduce a lightweight, two parameter recalibration method that adapts predictions to local patient populations using 50 to 200 labeled examples, reducing ECE to 0.007. Our findings establish open System One models as a promising zero shot baseline for medical AI, combining competitive predictive performance with low computational cost and efficient local calibration. We release our code and evaluation harness to support future research.
zh_abstract: System One决策模型（如Jev）在单次前向传递中回答结构化问题而不生成文本，提供快速且计算高效的临床决策支持。我们评估MedJev——一种可在笔记本电脑本地运行的开放式System One模型——在跨越医学知识、诊断和患者层面预测的十项医学基准上，使用MIMIC IV和MIMIC IV ED。我们将MedJev与零样本LLM基线、已发表的GPT结果以及监督模型进行比较。MedJev在MedQA上达到72.5%的准确率，在USMLE上达到75.4%，在NEJM上达到80.1%，接近已发表的GPT 4性能，同时保持校准良好的置信度估计（ECE 0.028至0.063）。在患者层面任务中，MedJev在院内死亡率（In Hospital Mortality）上达到0.926的AUROC，超过XGBoost（0.902），但在急诊分诊入院（ED Triage Admission）等运营结局上表现不及监督模型（0.745 vs. 0.809）。患者层面预测还表现出显著的校准不良（院内死亡率ECE 0.286）。我们引入一种轻量级、双参数的重校准方法，使用50至200个有标签样本使预测适应当地患者人群，将ECE降至0.007。我们的发现确立开放式System One模型作为医学AI有前景的零样本基线，将具有竞争力的预测性能与低计算成本和高效本地校准相结合。我们发布代码和评估工具（evaluation harness）以支持未来研究。

abstract: [The Journal of international medical research] Hepatitis remains a major global health challenge and an important contributor to liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and liver-related mortality worldwide. Early diagnosis, effective treatment selection, and accurate prognostic stratification remain critical unmet needs in clinical hepatology. Artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning and deep learning, has emerged as a promising approach to addressing these challenges through the integration and analysis of large-scale, heterogeneous biomedical datasets. This narrative review synthesizes advances in artificial intelligence applications in hepatitis research and clinical practice published over the past decade, organized across three clinical domains: diagnosis, treatment optimization, and prognosis prediction. In the diagnostic domain, artificial intelligence-based approaches have been applied to medical imaging, digital pathology, and multi-omics data to enhance the detection, classification, and staging of liver disease. In the therapeutic domain, machine learning models have been increasingly deployed to support drug discovery, optimize therapeutic regimens, and predict individual treatment responses. In the prognostic domain, artificial intelligence-driven models have shown promising performance in predicting disease progression, survival outcomes, and clinical complications. Nevertheless, key limitations persist, including data heterogeneity, limited external generalizability, and barriers to clinical translation. Future progress will depend on prospective multicenter evaluation, use of interoperable multimodal data, development of transparent models that account for uncertainty, and evidence that artificial intelligence improves clinical decisions and patient outcomes rather than performance metrics alone.
zh_abstract: ［《国际医学研究杂志》（The Journal of International Medical Research）］肝炎仍是全球重大健康挑战，也是全球肝纤维化、肝硬化、肝细胞癌和肝脏相关死亡的重要促成因素。早期诊断、有效治疗选择以及准确的预后分层仍是临床肝病学中关键且未被满足的需求。人工智能，尤其是机器学习和深度学习，通过整合和分析大规模、异质性生物医学数据集，已成为应对这些挑战的有前景的方法。本叙述性综述综合了过去十年发表的肝炎研究和临床实践中人工智能应用进展，按三个临床领域组织：诊断、治疗优化和预后预测。在诊断领域，基于人工智能的方法已应用于医学影像、数字病理学和多组学数据，以增强肝病的检测、分类和分期。在治疗领域，机器学习模型越来越多地被部署用于支持药物发现、优化治疗方案和预测个体治疗反应。在预后领域，人工智能驱动的模型在预测疾病进展、生存结局和临床并发症方面显示出有希望的性能。然而，关键局限性仍然存在，包括数据异质性、有限的外部可推广性以及临床转化障碍。未来的进展将取决于前瞻性多中心评估、使用可互操作的多模态数据、开发能够考虑不确定性的透明模型，以及证明人工智能改善临床决策和患者结局而不仅仅是性能指标的证据。

abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Scarborough Health Network; conditions: Patient Discharge, Health Literacy; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 52; status: RECRUITING] This randomized pilot study will compare standard hospital discharge communication with discharge summaries simplified using ContextCare, an artificial intelligence-assisted application. The study will enroll 50 adults discharged from Scarborough Health Network. Participants will be assigned to one of two groups in a 1:1 ratio, with allocation stratified by baseline health literacy. The main measure is how well participants explain their diagnosis, treatment, follow-up care, and instructions for seeking further help immediately after receiving discharge information. The study will also assess satisfaction, recall after discharge, and selected post-discharge outcomes.

abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Nantes University Hospital; conditions: Bacteremia; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 8765; status: COMPLETED] Bacteremia, a common infection associated with high morbidity and mortality, requires prompt and appropriate antibiotic treatment. Numerous studies have shown that the appropriate use of antibiotics helps improve the prognosis of patients, reduce the selection of pathogenic organisms, the emergence of antibiotic resistance, adverse treatment effects, and healthcare costs. The Nantes University Hospital Center has operated a Biomedical Data Warehouse (BDW) since 2018. The growing availability of data through BDWs thus enables the development of decision-support tools based on machine learning. The primary objective of the OPTIBact project is to predict the optimal empirical antibiotic for hospitalized patients with bacteremia using a machine learning-based predictive model using data from the Nantes University Hospital's BDW. As secondary objectives, the study aims: * To compare the performance of the predictive model for the optimal empirical antibiotic against standard patient care * To estimate the expected benefit of the predictive model compared to real-world practice in terms of clinical outcomes * To predict the optimal dosage of empirical antibiotic therapy * To compare the performance of the predictive model for optimal empirical antibiotic therapy dosing with standard patient care * To describe inpatient patients in Nantes University Hospital who received optimal antibiotic therapy and those who did not * To Identify predictors of antibiotic resistance in bacteria isolated from blood cultures, stratified by pathogen type.
zh_abstract: ［新注册临床试验，尚无结果；申办者：南特大学医院；疾病：菌血症；类型：观察性；入组人数：8765；状态：已完成］菌血症是一种常见感染，与高发病率和死亡率相关，需要及时且适当的抗生素治疗。大量研究表明，适当使用抗生素有助于改善患者预后，减少病原菌选择、抗生素耐药性的出现、不良治疗效应以及医疗费用。南特大学医院中心自2018年起运营生物医学数据仓库（Biomedical Data Warehouse, BDW）。因此，通过BDW可获得的数据日益增多，使得能够开发基于机器学习的决策支持工具。OPTIBact项目的主要目标是利用南特大学医院BDW的数据，使用基于机器学习的预测模型，预测住院菌血症患者的最佳经验性抗生素。作为次要目标，本研究旨在：* 将最佳经验性抗生素预测模型的性能与标准患者诊疗进行比较 * 估计该预测模型与真实世界实践相比在临床结局方面的预期获益 * 预测经验性抗生素治疗的最佳剂量 * 将最佳经验性抗生素治疗剂量预测模型的性能与标准患者诊疗进行比较 * 描述南特大学医院接受最佳抗生素治疗和未接受最佳抗生素治疗的住院患者 * 识别从血培养中分离的细菌的抗生素耐药预测因素，并按病原体类型分层。

abstract: [Dentistry journal] Background: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly growing in the field of dental medicine and in oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMS). The aim of the present review is to assess current applications of AI in OMS, to evaluate their advantages and limitations, and to identify areas requiring further research. Materials and Methods: A comprehensive search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, with targeted keywords including "artificial intelligence," "deep learning," "machine learning," "oral surgery," "maxillofacial surgery," and "diagnosis "Artificial Intelligence" OR "Machine Learning" OR "Deep Learning" AND "Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery" OR "Oral Surgery" OR "Maxillofacial Surgery" AND "Diagnosis". Of 308 identified studies, 37 met the inclusion criteria focusing on AI-assisted detection interpretation and surgical planning in OMS. Results: AI is effective in identifying anatomical landmarks, evaluating lesions and cysts, diagnosing bone disease like medication-related osteonecrosis of jaws (MRONJ), planning dental implants, and aiding in the classification of fractures and temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders. AI can match or outperform human experts in various diagnostic tasks, particularly in panoramic and cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) image analysis. AI shows promise in early detection of impacted and supernumerary teeth, maxillofacial pathologies, neoplastic conditions, and soft tissue calcifications. Limitations: However, substantial methodological heterogeneity, inconsistent reporting of AI performance metrics, and limited external validation across the included studies constrain direct comparison of results and assessment of the generalizability of reported AI performance. Conclusions: AI may assist clinicians in diagnostic and treatment-related decision-making, but current evidence does not support its use as a replacement for comprehensive clinical assessment and professional judgment.
zh_abstract: [牙科期刊]【背景】人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI）在牙医学以及口腔颌面外科（oral and maxillofacial surgery, OMS）领域的使用正在迅速增长。本综述旨在评估AI在OMS中的当前应用，评价其优势与局限性，并识别需要进一步研究的领域。【材料与方法】使用PubMed、Scopus和Google Scholar进行了全面检索，目标关键词包括“artificial intelligence”“deep learning”“machine learning”“oral surgery”“maxillofacial surgery”和“diagnosis ‘Artificial Intelligence’ OR ‘Machine Learning’ OR ‘Deep Learning’ AND ‘Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery’ OR ‘Oral Surgery’ OR ‘Maxillofacial Surgery’ AND ‘Diagnosis’”。在308项已识别研究中，37项符合纳入标准，聚焦于OMS中AI辅助的检测解读和手术规划。【结果】AI在识别解剖标志、评估病变和囊肿、诊断药物相关性颌骨坏死（medication-related osteonecrosis of jaws, MRONJ）等骨病、规划牙种植体以及辅助骨折和颞下颌关节（temporomandibular joint, TMJ）疾病分类方面有效。AI在各种诊断任务中可达到或超过人类专家，尤其是在全景和锥形束计算机断层扫描（cone-beam computed tomography, CBCT）图像分析中。AI在阻生牙和多生牙、颌面部病变、肿瘤性疾病以及软组织钙化的早期检测中显示出前景。【局限性】然而，纳入研究之间存在显著的方法学异质性、AI性能指标报告不一致以及外部验证有限，限制了结果的直接比较和对所报告AI性能泛化能力的评估。【结论】AI可能辅助临床医生进行诊断和治疗相关决策，但当前证据不支持将其作为全面临床评估和专业判断的替代。

title: Instability as Signal: Diagnosing Latent Heterogeneity in Multimodal Survival Models
zh_title: 多模态生存模型的不稳定性作为诊断信号
summary: 预印本以TCGA-BRCA多模态融合模型为探针，分析生存预测不稳定的来源并识别稳定潜在亚组。
abstract: Multimodal deep learning models for cancer survival prediction frequently exhibit unstable and irreproducible performance, limiting their clinical applicability. Rather than proposing a new predictive architecture, this work presents a diagnostic investigation into the sources of this instability. Using a transformer-based deep fusion model combining RNA sequencing and histopathology data from the TCGA-BRCA cohort as a diagnostic probe, we demonstrate that global survival prediction is highly unstable across data splits. We then analyze the learned multimodal embeddings in an unsupervised manner, revealing stable latent patient subgroups with significantly divergent survival outcomes. These subgroups are not explained by canonical receptor status or immune infiltration, but instead align with tumor-intrinsic proliferative activity. Conditioning survival modeling on the largest discovered subgroup recovers strong and stable prognostic performance, substantially outperforming unimodal baselines. These findings indicate that survival predictability is conditional on latent heterogeneity and suggest that heterogeneity-aware modeling strategies are essential for robust multimodal prognostication. This work establishes a methodological framework for interpreting instability in multimodal survival learning.

zh_abstract: 用于癌症生存预测的多模态深度学习模型经常表现出不稳定且不可重复的性能，限制了其临床适用性。本工作并非提出新的预测架构，而是对这种不稳定性的来源进行诊断性研究。我们使用一个基于Transformer的深度融合模型，该模型结合TCGA-BRCA队列的RNA测序和组织病理学数据，作为诊断探针，证明全局生存预测在不同数据划分间高度不稳定。然后，我们以无监督方式分析学习到的多模态嵌入，揭示了具有显著不同生存结局的稳定潜在患者亚组。这些亚组不能由经典受体状态或免疫浸润解释，而是与肿瘤内在的增殖活性一致。以发现的最大亚组为条件进行生存建模，可恢复强且稳定的预后性能，显著优于单模态基线。这些发现表明，生存可预测性以潜在异质性为条件，并提示异质性感知建模策略对于稳健的多模态预后至关重要。本工作为解释多模态生存学习中的不稳定性建立了一个方法学框架。

In most cases the AI does not work alone: a clinician makes the final decision, using the AI as support. Before these tools are used in the NHS, they must be tested to show they are safe and helpful. They are usually tested in a "reader study", where several clinicians each interpret the same set of images, sometimes with the AI's help and sometimes without, so performance can be compared. These studies tend to focus on whether the diagnosis was correct. However, accuracy alone may not measure everything that matters. For example, what happens when the AI gets it wrong, whether clinicians rely on it too much or too little, or how the tool affects efficiency. At present there is no agreed standard for what these studies should measure, so important things are often missed and studies are hard to compare. Aim: The aim of this study is to find out, by talking to people with different perspectives, which outcomes are important when evaluating AI tools that help clinicians read medical images. Objectives: 1. Explore which outcomes people think matter when judging whether an AI tools is safe and good enough to use 2. Understand the reasons behind their views 3. Explore how priorities differ between groups, such as patients and developers. The output will be a list of important candidate outcomes, which will feed into a future project to agree a recommended set of outcomes for these studies (a "core outcome set"). abstract: BackgroundClinical decision support systems (CDSS) are increasingly embedded in national telemedicine services, however how different stakeholders who use them experience these tools, particularly in low-and middle-income countries, is less explored. In the assisted model of Indias eSanjeevani service, spoke health workers enter structured symptoms and hub clinicians review a symptom summary and an artificial intelligence (AI)-generated differential diagnosis. ObjectiveTo describe role-specific experiences of eSanjeevanis CDSS functions and to estimate how acceptance coexists with specific reported difficulties within each role. MethodsWe analyzed a program feedback web survey completed between 11 July and 29 July, 2025 by hub clinicians and spoke providers. Prespecified item profiles covered review of summaries and suggested diagnoses, the perceived relation of suggestions to the clinicians own diagnosis, ease of use and intention to use (hub), and symptom-capture utility, question quantity, question relevance, summary presentation and satisfaction (spoke). Within-role contrasts were reported as absolute differences in acceptance with Newcombe 95% CIs. Short open comments underwent content analysis. ResultsThe cohort comprised 190 hub and 662 spoke respondents from 13 and 15 states (21.4% and 19.3% of eligible providers). Among hub respondents, 76.8% regularly reviewed the symptom summary and 58.9% the suggested diagnoses; 72.6% judged suggestions matched (32.6%) or appropriate but different (40.0%), 7.9% mostly inappropriate, and 11.1% reported that suggestions were mostly not generated. Overall, 85.3% intended to keep using the tools. Affirmative intention was 98.4% when suggestions matched, 66.7% when they were mostly inappropriate (difference vs matched or appropriate-23.2 percentage points, 95% CI-48.5 to-4.0) and 61.9% when mostly absent (-25.7, 95% CI-47.1 to-7.3); technical issues, reported by 38.4%, made little difference (-2.8, 95% CI-14.1 to 7.3). Among spoke respondents, 63.4% rated question quantity appropriate, with miscalibration in both directions (15.6% too many; 16.6% too few); 89.9% found the questions relevant and 91.8% found the summary clear. Satisfaction was 75.3% and did not differ materially between those reporting too many questions and those reporting an appropriate number (-2.7, 95% CI-12.8 to 6.0). abstract: Deep learning shows promise for breast cancer diagnosis, but limited interpretability hinders clinical adoption. We benchmark ten ImageNet-pretrained models (ResNet50, VGG19, InceptionV3, DenseNet121, Xception, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet, ConvNeXt, ViT, and Swin Transformer) for benign-versus-malignant classification on the BreakHis histopathology dataset using a patient-level split, and explain their predictions with Grad-CAM, LIME, Integrated Gradients, and LRP. DenseNet121 performed best, with 99.4% test accuracy and an AUC-ROC of 0.999, and significantly outperformed all other models (p < 0.001). Transformer-based models trailed the CNNs. The explanations consistently highlighted nuclei-rich and glandular regions of diagnostic relevance. Combining transfer learning with explainable AI can thus yield accurate, interpretable tools for breast cancer diagnosis.
zh_abstract: 深度学习在乳腺癌诊断中显示出前景，但有限的可解释性阻碍了临床采用。我们在BreakHis组织病理学数据集上，使用患者水平划分，对十种ImageNet预训练模型（ResNet50、VGG19、InceptionV3、DenseNet121、Xception、MobileNetV2、EfficientNet、ConvNeXt、ViT和Swin Transformer）进行良性与恶性分类的基准测试，并用Grad-CAM、LIME、Integrated Gradients和LRP解释其预测。DenseNet121表现最佳，测试准确率为99.4%，AUC-ROC为0.999，并显著优于所有其他模型（p < 0.001）。基于Transformer的模型落后于CNN。这些解释一致地突出了具有诊断相关性的富含细胞核区域和腺体区域。因此，将迁移学习与可解释AI相结合，可以产生准确、可解释的乳腺癌诊断工具。
